recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Restoring Media wording to Binary would reintroduce obsolete guidance; any future wording change should come from a new current-version issue about Binary/DocumentReference boundaries.
issue_request: FHIR-17025 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Binary change request asking Binary's Boundaries and Relationships section to explain how Binary relates to DocumentReference, Media, and FHIR Documents, including that DocumentReference/Media content is searchable while Binary is not.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14349, represented by git commit 6d889d86b413e655a0d9e033525a07a9ab9eee2d, which added the requested Binary boundaries paragraphs.
additional_context: Later commit 5c62f91cd81f150be72ad506c876e3cc20bd631d removed Media references from Binary as part of the GF#19250 Media-to-DocumentReference work. FHIR-38950 then copied Media-style boundary concepts into DocumentReference. Current R6 history records Media as removed with DocumentReference or Observation as replacements, and source/fhir.ini's active resource list includes Binary and DocumentReference but not Media.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Binary page still covers DocumentReference, Binary search limitations, and FHIR Documents as Bundle or sometimes Binary; current DocumentReference contains the media-file, audio/video/image, DICOM/WADO, and Binary-target guidance that replaced Media-era text.

related_jiras.note: Media-to-DocumentReference history explains why Media was removed from Binary boundaries text.
Copied Media boundaries concepts into DocumentReference after Media/DocumentReference consolidation.
